source.title: Adversarial Training with Large Step Sizes: Implicit Bias, Optimization, and Sharpness

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary text are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures sharpness during deterministic training and compares it with the edge-of-stability behavior named in V5, using neural-network experiments rather than the cited studies’ measurements.
record.gate_note: The empirical results report sharpness trajectories, not training classification error. The logistic-regression optimization results are about adversarial training and do not test a listed version. The cited prior-study results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures V5's sharpness dynamics using deterministic full-batch GD and MSE, reproduces standard-training comparisons, and tests extension to adversarial neural-network training. Adversarial training changes the objective but still measures the neural-network optimization behavior V5 names.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the empirical sharpness finding but omits the other main conclusions. The authors also establish robust max-margin implicit bias for adversarial logistic regression at arbitrary constant step sizes and show that uniform acceleration and eventual loss monotonicity can fail. Their neural-network experiments show initial sharpening followed by oscillations with declining long-term sharpness, differing from standard training's usual threshold-hovering pattern.
record.recipe_differences: Deterministic gradient descent with MSE on a 4 class, 1000 example CIFAR-10 subset; the compared V5 work studies large-learning-rate loss and sharpness dynamics in other settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The standard-training sharpness description has an explicit exception for MLP at step size 0.005. The authors state that adversarial sharpness behavior is consistent across architectures, datasets, attack-generation approaches, and step sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: For robustly separable adversarial logistic regression, GD approaches the robust max-margin direction for any fixed positive step size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adversarial logistic regression retains robust max-margin implicit bias under arbitrary constant step sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 4.2 constructs horizon-dependent adversarial logistic-regression datasets with a positive finite-horizon loss lower bound for every constant step size and infinitely many loss increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adversarial logistic regression need not admit uniform optimization acceleration or eventual monotone loss under constant-step GD.

fits_no_version.finding: The adversarial Huber toy objective has limiting sharpness O(η + c²) under the specified initialization and boundary assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A min-max Huber regression model can converge far below the standard edge-of-stability sharpness level.

record.problems: The relevant trajectories are presented as figures without numerical sharpness values or uncertainty estimates. The paper reports an exception for the MLP at step size 0.005. Its experiments use a 4 class, 1000 example subset of CIFAR-10, and do not measure training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were omitted. The adversarial-training sharpness results do not map to a listed version, and their figure-only values are not separately extracted here.

untested.parts: Training classification error across model sizes, corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, and the specified SGD/Adam recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and the effect of extra student neurons.
Controlled depth comparisons of plain and residual networks, longer training, special tanh initialization, and Fixup.
Controlled initialization comparisons, signal and gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.

Loss recovery after exceeding the initial linearized stability limit, divergence at larger rates, and divergence despite starting below the threshold. R2–R4 establish sharpness behavior without separately establishing simultaneous standard-training loss decrease.
Controlled batch-normalization comparisons, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training speed and stability.

missing.what: Standard-training MLP results at step sizes other than 0.005: the Figure 2 caption includes these in the reported edge-of-stability pattern, but R1 records only the exception.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Its adversarial neural-network sharpness and loss results bear on V5 and should be reclassified from fits_no_version. They are explicitly declared omitted in rows_left_out, so they are not additionally listed as missing; the corresponding verdict rests on the supplied text. Adversarial sharpness holds generated inputs fixed when computing the parameter Hessian, which limits interpretation as curvature of the complete min-max objective. Figure images and individual curve values are unavailable in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random initialization, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 label corruption, and model size.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and student width.
Plain versus residual network training error across depth; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.

The paper measures sharpness but does not report numerical values for individual curves; it does not test loss recovery above a stability limit, divergence at larger rates, or the claimed longer-time sharpness behavior in full-batch training.
